trust_decision.summary: Whether a fake()/fakeEval expression may traverse a function-valued entrypoint (implicitly invoking it) and then read an arbitrary key from that call's result, and whether such a lookup must be re-checked through resolveProperty instead of being done inline; decided in resolveProperty's 'function' branch.

landing_point.why: The advisory names helpers.fake(); fake() at 1267-1295 is the only caller of fakeEval and is where an engineer reading only the summary starts.

fix_sites.entry_point: faker.helpers.fake(pattern) (string or array of patterns) -> fakeEval -> resolveProperty
fix_sites.module_kind: internal helper module (fakeEval is not exported from src/index.ts; only the HelpersModule type is public)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The implicit invocation is documented and tested behaviour (fakeEval('airline.airline.iataCode') is listed as supported at src/modules/helpers/eval.ts:46 and asserted at test/modules/helpers-eval.spec.ts:110), so a solver can argue the call-then-read path is intended and leave resolveProperty as it is.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Implicitly invoking a function-valued entrypoint and reading a key off its result is legitimate and tested: fake('{{airline.airline.iataCode}}') and fake('{{string.numeric}}') must keep returning data, and fake('{{airline.airline}}') must still stringify to '[object Object]' (test/modules/helpers.spec.ts:1045-1054, 970-973). A fix that stops calling functions, or refuses property access on a call result, breaks all of these.

O6_input_shapes: array of patterns (one element chosen at src/modules/helpers/index.ts:1269)
property after an implicit function reference (airline.airline.iataCode)
multi-hop path where the call result is itself a function (lazy chain), which the fix now resolves
key lookup on a primitive call result, which the fix now resolves to undefined instead of walking the wrapper prototype

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The substituted value is re-scanned by a recursive fake() call, so a value that itself contains '{{...}}' is evaluated in a second pass.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The recursion exists to resolve multiple tokens; a maintainer plausibly added it without a guard that produced values are not re-parsed, which is a natural sibling of the same resolve-expression mechanism.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: helpers.mustache() resolves '{{key}}' from a data record and invokes function-valued entries through String.replace.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is documented as the custom-function alternative to fake() in the same module, so a maintainer extending fake()'s resolution rules would plausibly touch it too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: evalProcessFunction invokes any function entrypoint with attacker-supplied parameters.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the call half of the same mechanism; an allow-list of callable entrypoints is the kind of guard a maintainer could add next to resolveProperty.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Locale categories are merged with object spread, so a function-valued entry nested inside a category survives while a function used as a whole category value is silently reduced to '{}'.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Locale data is the only place lazy function entries come from; a maintainer hardening lazy definitions could plausibly normalise or reject them here.

O9_family: CWE-95 improper neutralization of directives in dynamically evaluated code (unsafe property-path resolution in helpers.fake)

O10_build.project_tests: test/modules/helpers-eval.spec.ts (fakeEval unit tests, 20 cases); test/modules/helpers.spec.ts:964-1130 (fake() behaviour); test/all-functional.spec.ts:140-160 (every module method through fake() for all locales)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Blacklist dangerous keys ('constructor', '__proto__', 'prototype') or drop the implicit function call inside resolveProperty, which leaves the call-then-read path unfixed and breaks fake('{{airline.airline.iataCode}}').

out_of_scope_notes: helpers.mustache() (src/modules/helpers/index.ts:727-748) invokes function values of its data record through String.replace; that is documented API for caller-supplied data, not the same sink as fakeEval, and was not pursued.

The advisory's arbitrary-code-execution claim could not be located in this tree: every function reached during resolution is invoked before any key is read, so no path from a fake() expression to the Function constructor was traced in resolveProperty.
unverified: repo_mb: size not measured (no shell in this session); src/locales dominates the tree, so tiny_repo/giant_repo were left out.

Whether the fix's added test (fakeEval('custom.lazy.key') with a lazy definition) actually fails at the pinned commit: hand-tracing suggests it may already pass, because the last resolution hop calls the function and then reads the key; the observable delta of the fix appears to be only a function whose call result is itself a function, plus no more prototype traversal of primitive results.
Public writeups, release notes and the GHSA text beyond the one-line summary (no network); recall risk is an estimate.
Whether hidden behavioural tests would be derived from the added test at fix.diff:26-35 or newly written for the deeper lazy chain.
